definitions.explanation: An authoritative directive that must be followed.
The grammatical form used for commands.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}から{命令|めいれい}を{受|う}けた。
examples.english: I received an order from my boss.

examples.japanese: {命令|めいれい}に{従|したが}わなければならない。
{社長|しゃちょう}が{全員|ぜんいん}に{残業|ざんぎょう}を{命令|めいれい}した。
examples.english: The company president ordered everyone to work overtime.

examples.japanese: {裁判所|さいばんしょ}から{退去|たいきょ}{命令|めいれい}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: An eviction order was issued by the court.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{部下|ぶか}に{命令|めいれい}ばかりして、{自分|じぶん}では{何|なに}もしない。
examples.english: He does nothing but order his subordinates around and doesn't do anything himself.

examples.japanese: {命令形|めいれいけい}を{使|つか}って{文|ぶん}を{作|つく}りなさい。
examples.english: Make sentences using the imperative form.

examples.japanese: 「{食|た}べろ」は「{食|た}べる」の{命令形|めいれいけい}です。
{日本語|にほんご}の{命令形|めいれいけい}は{男性|だんせい}が{使|つか}うことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: The imperative form in Japanese is more often used by men.

examples.japanese: {命令文|めいれいぶん}は{相手|あいて}に{直接|ちょくせつ}{行動|こうどう}を{求|もと}める{表現|ひょうげん}だ。
examples.english: An imperative sentence is an expression that directly demands action from the listener.

examples.japanese: {命令|めいれい}の{口調|くちょう}は{目上|めうえ}の{人|ひと}に{使|つか}ってはいけない。
examples.english: You must not use a commanding tone with people above you in status.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{命令|めいれい}する (to order, to command)
・{命令|めいれい}を{出|だ}す (to issue an order)
・{命令|めいれい}を{受|う}ける (to receive an order)
・{命令|めいれい}に{従|したが}う (to obey an order)
・{命令|めいれい}に{背|そむ}く (to disobey an order)

GRAMMAR TERM:
・{命令形|めいれいけい} (imperative form)
・{命令文|めいれいぶん} (imperative sentence)

RELATED WORDS:
・{指示|しじ} (instruction, direction - softer)
・{指令|しれい} (order, command - formal/military)
・{お{願|ねが}い (request - polite alternative)
